slides.title: Claude Code (CC) vs OpenClaw (OC) Why people
slides.text: Claude Code (CC) vs OpenClaw (OC) Why people are so excited about openclaw? The vision of a "live" assistant that "my mom can use" is exciting But right now to work with OC you need to be technical and VERY careful But if you are can use Claude Code, then for any particular task you can ask it to create a combination of skills and scripts. Then you can run this on your personal laptop and can schedule it to run on a regular basis. It is safe. You can have persistent memory, work with local docs, work with websites This way you can get almost all functionality you need for your daily tasks. And you can use your Claude subscription (which is not available for OpenClaw because of Anthropic's recent ban) You can set up a small server for webhooks You can switch to use only local model(s) for extra privacy How OpenClaw is different? OpenClaw is designed to run 24/7 to communicate on multiple channels (WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, email, etc.), maintain long‑lived sessions It provides a central framework (an "Agent OS") to run your tasks - a workflow engine with triggers, conditions, actions; "universal inbox" for chat channels and external content, plus stateful context and memory; So why some people are excited about OpenClaw? Because they want a universal personal assistant - not a dev tool; They are aiming for “it clears my inbox, texts me reminders, books flights, etc., on its own,” across accounts and devices. They want to have a system which already has all pieces wired together - cron, webhooks, a message bus, a skill runner, and state persistence, chat routing across WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack/iMessage), a plugin registry with 50+ integrations; Session/context/memory and tool sandboxing built in. The excitement is: “finally a general agent OS I can self‑host and extend,” not “finally something I couldn’t hack together myself with Claude + cron.” OpenClaw is mostly a convenience abstraction and ecosystem, not a fundamental capability unlock If you’re comfortable wiring small servers, cron, scripts, and skills, then with Claude Code you can have “run on my laptop, with my own scripts” setup which gives you very good control over privacy But if you ever decide to expose agents over WhatsApp/Telegram/Slack for other people, build shared assistants for a team or customers, or want a unified “agent OS” with plugins and message routing baked in, then something like OpenClaw (or whatever replaces/competes with it) starts to make more sense Anthropic's 11 new plugins for Claude Co-work https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dVpIPXmEk8Y All plugins are free, open-source, and shareable via zip files Users can customize existing plugins or build entirely new ones using plain English descriptions through the meta "plugin management" plugin Plugins are for sales, marketing, legal, finance, customer support, ... , for example: contract review with risk flagging, sales pipeline management, and automated workflow creation. Each plugin contains three components: skills (automatic background knowledge), commands (triggered workflows using slash commands), connectors (integrations with existing software).

slides.title: You Could've Invented OpenClaw You Could've Invented OpenClaw
slides.text: You Could've Invented OpenClaw You Could've Invented OpenClaw - by Nader Dabit, Feb 10 Building a mini-openclaw.py in 400 lines of python https://nader.substack.com/p/you-couldve-invented-openclaw OpenClaw is just a clean composition of simple building blocks: sessions, system prompts, tools, queues, cron, and multi-channel I/O They are stitched together into a persistent multi-agent assistant that runs on your own hardware Start with a trivial Telegram echo bot Add disk-backed JSONL sessions so the assistant remembers prior messages Add a “SOUL” system personality prompt (Jarvis) Add a tools API (run commands, read/write files, web search) with an agent loop that lets the LLM emit tool calls, execute them, and iterate until it’s ready to answer Add a persistent approval system to prevent dangerous shell execution Add gateway to use multiple transports (http, Telegram, ...) Add context compaction (summarizing old transcript halves) Add long‑term markdown memory with save/search tools Add per-session locks for safe concurrency Add cron-based “heartbeats” for scheduled tasks Add multiple agents (e.g. main vs research) with different SOULs, models, and session prefixes that share a common memory store The Ultimate Guide to OpenClaw https://corpwaters.substack.com/p/the-ultimate-guide-to-openclaw GitHub - 232K Stars, Release 2026.2.25 https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw

slides.title: Matthew Berman's AI Employee Matt uses Agents SDK
slides.text: Matthew Berman's AI Employee Matt uses Agents SDK to use his Anthropic Max subscription. While Anthropic banned the use of personal Claude subscriptions via OAuth for external products, their Agents SDK remains a valid and effective alternative By converting his system to use the Agents SDK, he is able to continue leveraging his Anthropic Pro/Max subscription without facing token bans Here is the workflow he implemented: He created a centralized `anthropic-agent-sdk.js` file to handle all calls Token Resolution - The system resolves the OAuth token from its storage location to authenticate the session He wrapped all calls with auto-retry mechanisms, logging support, and prompt caching to maintain efficiency Centralized Routing - He built an `LLM-router.js` to manage traffic, allowing him to easily switch between the Anthropic Agents SDK and other providers like OpenAI's Codex SDK This approach has allowed him to use billions of tokens across his automated tasks (like CRM updates and email drafting) while staying within the terms of his subscription Matt spreads the jobs (because subscription has token cap every 5 hours) Matthew Berman Created OpenClaw F/T Employee Manages a dedicated sponsorship email address, using a sophisticated rubric to score leads, conduct background research on companies, and draft context-aware replies. It integrates deeply with tools like HubSpot for CRM tracking, Telegram for real-time notifications, and Fathom for meeting intelligence. Berman also shares advanced technical strategies, including "dual prompt stacks" to optimize performance across different AI models and a three-layer security defense against prompt injections Other key use cases mentioned include automated content pipelines, financial tracking via QuickBooks, and personalized health coaching By leveraging cron jobs for overnight processing and local embeddings to save costs, Berman demonstrates a highly efficient, autonomous AI ecosystem for business productivity https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3110hx3ygp0

slides.title: Liam Ottley - AI Business Models Liam Ottley
slides.text: Liam Ottley - AI Business Models Liam Ottley - Business Models https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KAufsCas_F4 OpenClaude is labeled as "iPhone moment for AI" It creates many business opportunities around providing skills and services for OpenClaude users From SaaS to "AI Skill Businesses": Traditional SaaS required massive work on interfaces, hosting, and security. But with AI assistants like OpenClaw, the assistant itself becomes the interface, allowing creators to focus solely on functionality and sell them on marketplaces like Clawhub Five Types of AI Skill Businesses: 1. Pure Prompt Skills - selling simple text files packaging expert instructions (e.g., how to review a legal contract) 2. Utility Skills - Code-based scripts that perform tasks like high-quality YouTube transcription or web scraping 3. API Integration Skills - Teaching the AI how to interact with existing tools like HubSpot or CRM systems 4. Backend Service Skills (Skills as a SaaS) - running a private server that does heavy lifting (like deep company research) while the user interacts through the AI assistant for a monthly fee 5. Proprietary Data Skills - AI provides insights based on a private, high-value database that others cannot access The risks: Technical Volatility - companies like Google and OpenAI will likely release competing platforms, potentially making current skills obsolete overnight Security Concerns - current open-source tools have significant security and compliance hurdles that prevent large businesses from adopting them yet Recommendation - focus on "boring" but proven AI consulting and agency work (the "rock") rather than purely chasing shiny new tech trends The Rock - "AI Agency" model: AI Auditing and Consulting - analyze company's roles and processes, find automation opportunities to get max return on investment Building and implementing AI automations and solutions. Especially using No-Code and Low-Code Automation Training teams and ensuring that AI tools are actually adopted and used effectively Building Long-term Relationships, focus on slow-moving problems that will exist for the next decade, such as how humans integrate new tech into legacy systems Liam is automating up to 70% of his business operations using Claude Code (not OpenClaw) - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O_VBdNrX0PM He builds layers of AI automation around existing business models, starting with a "Context OS" foundation and adding modules for data management, meeting intelligence, productivity tracking, and communication handling. The system operates through Telegram his method doesn't require extensive technical skills

slides.title: AI Updates Taalas chips - 17,000 Tok/sec inference
slides.text: AI Updates Taalas chips - 17,000 Tok/sec inference https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WjxOffC2kyM Taalas, a new startup, has created a chip that can process 17,000 tokens per second using an embedded Llama 3.1  8B params model All layers/weights are hardcoded inside the chip. No external CPU, GPU, or memory is needed. The chip uses mostly 3-bit quantization (some sensitive areas use 6-bit quantization). Company raised $200 Million Chinese AI Firms Distill Anthropic’s Claude Models Anthropic reported that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, and MiniMax ran “industrial-scale” distillation attacks against its Claude models, issuing over 16 million queries via roughly 24,000 fraudulent accounts , often routed through commercial proxy networks to evade detection The community and figures like Elon Musk have labeled Anthropic as hypocrites. Critics point out that Anthropic has also been accused of training its models on stolen or copyrighted data Elon Musk stated that Anthropic is "guilty of stealing training data at massive scale" and has paid multi-billion dollar settlements for it. Tech analysts argue the data volumes cited by Anthropic are too low to constitute a massive theft, suggesting they might simply reflect standard benchmarking - https://x.com/AnthropicAI/status/2025997928242811253

slides.title: AI Updates ChatGPT upgrade to its deep research
slides.text: AI Updates ChatGPT upgrade to its deep research feature https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XmKD8BGiC8w Providing significantly more granular control and access to over 60 different apps including Expedia, Zillow, Slack, and Stripe. Users can now specify which websites to search or exclude, connect various third-party applications, and interrupt research mid-process to add adjustments or follow-up questions. The enhanced version performs hundreds of searches with detailed citations, creating comprehensive reports with graphs, charts, and exportable formats to Word or PDF. While taking longer than the legacy version (20-40+ minutes), it enables powerful use cases like analyzing flight price trends through Expedia data or researching real estate markets via Zillow integration. This upgrade allows businesses to generate detailed reports, making it substantially more powerful than other platforms' research capabilities ChatGPT update called interactive code blocks Allows users to write, run, and fix code directly within the chat interface https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=znIj4XPsHak Previously, users had to copy and paste code into external tools. Now you can click preview to see your code run live, use split-screen mode to edit code while watching real-time updates, and build functional apps, landing pages, calculators, and diagrams without external tools or developer skills. The update eliminates the need for copying between applications and enables rapid prototyping for marketers, coaches, agency owners, and content creators. Users can build business tools like lead magnets, member dashboards, and interactive content in minutes rather than hours, making AI-powered development accessible to non-technical users and significantly lowering barriers to building digital products.

slides.title: Run OpenClaw on your Mac Safely Run OpenClaw
slides.text: Run OpenClaw on your Mac Safely Run OpenClaw on your Mac Safely by isolating it, limiting its access, locking down network exposure https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9AxdzsVkMLI https://levelup.gitconnected.com/you-dont-need-to-buy-a-mac-mini-to-run-openclaw-27bd564c0c9d Step 1: Install OpenClaw cleanly (homebrew + node.js - then install OpenClaw via the official CLI or installer for macOS https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YSJ61RiO7As Keep OpenClaw updated to get security fixes Step 2: Isolate from your main account - create a separate standard macOS user just for OpenClaw and run it only there https://us.ugreen.com/blogs/docking-stations/openclaw-on-mac-mini Store projects in a dedicated folder (for example `~/ai-workspace`) and avoid linking cloud drives into that account Step 3: Restrict what it can touch - Do not grant access to ~/.ssh, ~/Library/Keychains, or ~/.gnupg; keep secrets out of its user profile Treat ~/.openclaw as sensitive (contains API keys and long‑term memory files) Step 4: Lock down networking - Configure OpenClaw to bind only to `127.0.0.1` and set an auth token for the gateway. https://bitlaunch.io/blog/install-configure-openclaw/ Use Tailscale encrypted tunnel for remote access instead of exposing ports publicly https://help.apiyi.com/en/openclaw-local-vs-server-deployment-guide-en.html Optional: Extra isolation by running a separate macOS VM using UTM and install OpenClaw inside that VM Eventually rent VPS (Hostinger) or buy Mac Mini - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kqkOFKmNY_w Mac sandbox-exec user profile: (allow default) (allow network-outbound) (deny network-inbound (local tcp "*:*")) (deny file-write* (subpath "/")) (allow file-write* (subpath (string-append (param "HOME") "/.openclaw")) (subpath (string-append (param "HOME") "/.openclaw/workspace")) (subpath "/tmp")) (allow file-read*) # launch OpenClaw like this: sandbox-exec -f ~/.openclaw/sandbox.sb \ -D HOME=$HOME \ openclaw gateway --port 18789 # test: openclaw agent -m "hello"

slides.title: AI Updates Why AI generate Garbage Code -
slides.text: AI Updates Why AI generate Garbage Code - and How to Fix It https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7oRBHxMvWxQ Vicious cycle: AI produces large volumes of low-quality code that increases complexity, eventually slowing down development and leading to more errors To combat this, Bereznitsky proposes the following process: Research - scan the codebase to identify only relevant files Create architectural diagrams (C4, sequence, data flow) before writing any code Break the task into verifiable phases with clear quality criteria Implementation using a "team" of agents (including specialized roles for security, testing, and architecture review to validate the code against established standards India announced three (3) domestically-built models Sorum AI introduced two MoE models (30B & 105B params) optimized for 22 Indian languages and efficient enough to run on low-end devices. The government also unveiled Bhajan Pram 2, a 17B params  multimodal model for public sector use. Like DeepSeek's impact on assumptions about frontier AI development, India is demonstrating that sovereign AI development can serve 1.4 billion people largely ignored by global models, particularly through voice-first interfaces in regional languages. VoiceBox Open-source local-first AI voice cloning Powered by Alibaba’s Qwen2-72B It can clone a voice from just 3 sec of audio Stories Editor for multi-track audio production, built-in transcription via Whisper and a REST API for developers Runs entirely on your machine (Mac or Windows), ensuring total data privacy and no API limits https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=woQe90k7g3c

slides.title: AI Updates Modeling human concept formation, understanding and
slides.text: AI Updates Modeling human concept formation, understanding and communication Paper in "Nature Computational Science" Researchers introduced CATS-Net , a neural network framework designed to simulate how the human brain creates and uses abstract concepts. The model uses two modules: one to extract low-dimensional mental representations from sensory data and another to perform complex tasks using those concepts . The study found that CATS-Net’s internal "concept spaces" closely match actual human neural activity and semantic-control networks. By demonstrating how the brain decouples abstract thought from direct sensory input, this research provides a unified computational bridge between biological cognition and artificial intelligence. This framework helps explain how humans generalize knowledge and offers a path toward developing more flexible, human-like AI systems. https://www.nature.com/articles/s43588-026-00956-4

slides.title: AI Updates Claude Code Agent Modeling Trading Kris
slides.text: AI Updates Claude Code Agent Modeling Trading Kris made an agent to do trading https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yqr2qoTcMPk Google Builds Self-Learning AI (RL2F) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hm9WsUS6UH8 Reinforcement Learning with Language Feedback (RL2F) that enables self-improving AI systems. The new approach combines a teacher-student model structure where during training the teacher provides natural language feedback rather than direct answers. At inference time, the external teacher is removed and the model becomes auto-didactic, alternating between generating solutions, critiquing itself, and refining answers. Testing on mathematical problems showed significant performance improvements, with smaller models nearly matching larger ones through this self-learning capability.

slides.title: AI Updates GGML.ai (Georgi Gerganov + team) acquired
slides.text: AI Updates GGML.ai (Georgi Gerganov + team) acquired by Hugging Face GGML.ai is the team behind the GGML format and llama.cpp, the technology used to run LLMs The core projects remain open source and independent. Their repositories and licenses are not changing, and llama.cpp will continue to be developed in the open with community contributions The idea is to combine Hugging Face’s model hub and Transformers ecosystem with llama.cpp’s highly optimized local inference runtime This creates a stronger foundation for running AI models entirely on local hardware, with better tooling and long‑term maintenance The phrase “local AI’s long‑term home” reflects a bet that many AI workloads will increasingly run locally, and that the HF + GGML/llama.cpp stack will be the main open platform https://ggml.ai https://github.com/ggml-org/ggml https://github.com/ggml-org https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp Georgi Gerganov David Silver starts Ineffable Intelligence David Silver is DeepMind veteran, best known for leading the AlphaGo and AlphaZero projects, has left Google DeepMind to found a London-based startup called Ineffable Intelligence Goal - building superhuman or “endlessly learning” intelligence using reinforcement learning and world models rather than LLMs Silver is raising ~ $1 Bln in a seed round ($4B valuation) Silver’s stated view is that LLMs are fundamentally limited because they are trained on human-generated text, while agents that learn directly from experience in rich environments can, in principle, discover new knowledge and capabilities beyond what humans have written down. slides.title: AI Updates He Copied Warren Buffett's 'Free' Trap
slides.text: AI Updates He Copied Warren Buffett's 'Free' Trap and Made Millions https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EuXMn67uSME Young Warren Buffett - placed machines in barbershops for free, splitting profits 50-50 and reinvesting earnings to expand Leo used similar approach - offered free water for life in exchange for a $150 refundable deposit for water dispensers, quickly signing up 2,000 families and generating $300,000 in cash flow He used this money to buy stakes in filter and bucket factories and get 80% discounts on jugs The deposits generated enough interest to cover operational costs while creating customer lock-in. Both strategies demonstrate using "free" as bait to generate cash flow and leverage, controlling supply chains rather than competing on price, and letting other people's money work for them. Become an AI HACKER https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_yfiUQSbdPY New job/consulting market - hack AI systems Bug bounties, competitions, AI penetration testing Key techniques include prompt injection attacks, system prompt extraction, and exploiting AI chains to access confidential data

slides.text: AI Updates Make money by Helping others make money https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5PKYfRofUdg 1. Tie your work directly to revenue generation 2. Sell to people who actually have money (businesses rather than consumers) 3. Price based on value created rather than time spent 4. Develop skills that sit close to revenue like sales and marketing In capitalism, market value differs from societal value, which explains why teachers and social workers earn less than finance professionals despite their social importance. Tutorial How to Build an OpenClaw Business https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nSBKCZQkmYw Nat has created an AI assistant named Felix that has built a profitable business. Nat gave Felix access to various APIs including Vercel, Stripe, and GitHub, then tasked it with creating a product overnight. Felix developed a PDF guide on setting up OpenClaw systems, launched it at felixcraft.ai, and generated over $3,500 in sales within four days. The AI now has its own Twitter account with 2,500 followers and manages nearly $100,000 in cryptocurrency from trading fees. Key technical improvements include a three-layer memory system using QMD indexing, nightly memory consolidation, and separate Telegram group chats for different projects.
